title: Investigate and mitigate per-tenant heatmap count fade after late backfills
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Symptoms: Several customers reported that the Console hourly heatmap and stacked per-model area charts show a progressive 'fade' in counts for older hours after we applied a backfill for late streaming events. The fade manifests as a smooth decline in token/req counts across 2–12 hours back from the backfilled window, not raw spikes. This causes customer confusion and incorrect SLA/billing reconciliation for affected tenants.

Scope: Affects per-tenant/hour and per-model/hour aggregated series displayed in the Console and exported CSVs when a backfill job with deduplication runs for delayed telemetry. Likely triggered when a late-event backfill overlaps with the real-time smoothing and sampling layers used for charting and anomaly suppression.

Goal: Identify the root cause, implement a fix that preserves accuracy for backfilled windows without regressing chart noise or performance, and run a targeted re-aggregation of impacted tenant windows. Provide clear Console indicators for backfilled data and an ops playbook for future backfills.
acceptance_criteria: Root cause identified with a reproducible test case demonstrating fade effect
Correction implemented in aggregation/smoothing pipeline with unit/integration tests
Affected tenants re-aggregated and Console charts validated against raw ledger export
Backfill runs annotated in Console UI and CSV exports with a 'backfilled' flag
Rollout plan reviewed and signed off by Observability and Billing owners
steps: Reproduce locally: run late-event backfill on staging with the same ingestion pipeline and smoothing configuration
Add high-fidelity logging to the smoothing stage to capture event timestamps, tag origin (realtime vs backfill), and normalization factors
Audit deduplication: verify dedupe keys combine event_id + source_tag + tenant to ensure backfill doesn't create partial matches
Implement fix: change smoothing from multi-pass symmetric rolling average to causal exponential filter with normalization that ignores backfilled points for state initialization
Add 'backfilled' boolean flag on aggregated buckets and update Console rendering to display a subtle hatch on affected time ranges
Rebuild aggregates for tenants flagged in incident using the corrected pipeline (run in dry-run then live), and compare against raw ledger exports
Create and publish postmortem and an ops runbook for backfill procedures to avoid recurrence
notes: Preliminary hypothesis: existing symmetric smoothing expects uniformly arriving events; late backfill creates a spike that the symmetric filter spreads backward, producing the perceived fade
Related historical tickets mention similar windowing problems but with shard clock skew; this differs because the pattern is smooth and correlated to explicit backfill timestamps
We should avoid disabling smoothing globally — that will increase noise for customers with real-time bursty traffic
Will coordinate with Billing on whether rebuilt aggregates require customer-facing billing adjustments
Performance: causal filter should be O(n) with constant memory; need to validate end-to-end latency on large tenant aggregates
initial_findings: Reproduced on staging by replaying late events: heatmap shows backward smear up to 8 hours depending on backfill volume
Smoothing module uses a symmetric Hann-style window with endpoint padding based on 'current' wall-clock bucket counts — padding pulls backfilled mass into earlier buckets
Deduplication logic currently hashes on (user_event_id, model_alias) but backfill sources re-emitted events with new agent_id leading to partial dedupe; causes inconsistent normalization factors
Some tenants see larger effect because they have aggressive sampling turned on for live ingest; sampling rate is applied before smoothing which amplifies normalization errors
proposed_patch_refs: Change smoothing to 'causal_exponential' and add 'ignore_for_init' tag for backfilled buckets: PR #12458 (draft)
Fix dedupe to include 'ingest_source_id' in hash and add idempotency token in backfill job metadata: PR #12462
Migration job to rebuild 7 days of per-tenant aggregates: job id job-agg-rebuild-2026-03-11
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Changing smoothing might increase alert noise. Mitigation: feature flag rollout + monitoring of noise metrics for a small tenant cohort
Risk: Re-aggregating large tenants may take hours and be costly. Mitigation: run dry-run with checksum comparison and throttle concurrency; priorize high-impact tenants
Risk: Billing divergence after correction. Mitigation: coordinate with Billing and CS before final re-aggregation and offer reconciliation if needed
communication: Notified affected customers via CS ticket #CS-19821; template drafted for status updates
Slack channel #eng-usage-accuracy created for real-time coordination
